subject: Incident-driven erase authorization & log escrow playbook
messages:
From: Lena Huang <lena@meditech.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@meditech.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify: emergency erase + proof of deletion for subset of PHI

Hi Rishi,

We had an incident last week where a small batch of test PHI was mistakenly ingested into a sandbox tied to our integration. Our legal team is asking for an emergency erase confirmation and proof-of-deletion for affected records, plus a short-term log escrow snapshot so they can audit the sequence of events.

Can Redwood provide:
- A one-off erase run for the specified tenant scope with a signed attestation?
- The exact timestamp windows (start/end) and the operator IDs that executed the delete?
- A read-only log snapshot (safeguarded, SFTP or presigned link) capturing API request IDs for the retention window 2026-06-20 to 2026-06-27?

We understand this is outside normal SLA. Please advise the fastest path and any required DPA amendment or subprocessor evidence.

Thanks,
Lena Huang
Head of Compliance
Meditech Health

Attachment: incident_manifest.json (stub)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Lena Huang <lena@meditech.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: emergency erase + proof of deletion for subset of PHI

Hi Lena — thanks for flagging and very sorry this happened. We can support an incident-driven erase and provide the artifacts you listed, but there are a few dependencies:

1) Scope confirmation: we need the tenant ID + list of dataset IDs you want targeted (or a hashed ID set).
2) Legal attestation: we can produce a Redwood-signed attestation of the erase but legal will want an amendment that documents the special one-off run and limited escrow access.
3) Log escrow snapshot: we can generate a read-only archive of API and audit logs for the requested window. Delivery options: encrypted SFTP or presigned object with 14-day access.
4) Operator traceability: we will provide operator IDs and job-run metadata; redactions may apply for internal account IDs per our privacy policy.

Proposed timeline (accelerated):
- 06/28 EOD: scope confirmed by Meditech
- 06/29: ops runbook drafted and legal acceptance from both sides
- 06/30: erase execution + signed attestation + log archive delivered

I have looped in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and Laura (ops) to confirm feasibility and any chargeable work. If you prefer a locked-down process, we can run under an NDA addendum and produce the log snapshot via escrow SFTP.

Action items for Meditech: confirm tenant/dataset list and preferred delivery method for archive.

- Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Office: +1 415 555 0198

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, Lena Huang <lena@meditech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: emergency erase + proof of deletion for subset of PHI

Lena,

Quick legal/controls note: we can provide the attestation and the logs as described but will need Meditech to sign a scoped amendment to the DPA that:
- Authorizes a one-off emergency erase outside standard retention schedules
- Authorizes temporary access to immutable logs for audit (14-day window)
- Confirms acceptance of redaction rules for internal operator identifiers

If that's acceptable I will prepare a 1-page amendment and a short checklist for operations (attached: log-escrow-checklist.pdf).

Operational caveats for Laura/Markus:
- Erase will run against the tenant's object store and internal caches; we need to ensure KV-cache invalidation to prevent rehydration.
- Backups: we will need to create a policy to sweep the relevant backup shards to prevent reappearance in scheduled purges; this will be coordinated as an exception.
- Snapshot: ops will produce a time-bound, read-only snapshot and a hash manifest (meditech_erase_matrix_v1.xlsx attached) verifying files included.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 28, 2026 at 11:03 AM Rishi wrote:
> Hi Lena — thanks for flagging and very sorry this happened...

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Lena Huang <lena@meditech.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-30T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: emergency erase + proof of deletion for subset of PHI

Hi Lena — ops can execute the run on 2026-06-30 as long as Meditech confirms scope this morning. To keep everything auditable we will:

- Run a targeted erase job with an immutable job ID and operator sign-off.
- Quarantine any affected backup shards and run a coordinated purge pass during the next backup cycle, with an explicit tombstone and manifest in the escrow snapshot.
- Deliver: signed erase attestation (PDF), operator-run log extract (CSV), and a SHA256 manifest for each file in the escrow snapshot.

Delivery options:
- Preferred: encrypted SFTP transfer to meditech-provenance.meditech-sftp.redwood (requires IP allowlist)
- Alternate: presigned object links (14 days) + separate key share via DocuSign for attestation signatures

Cost note: accelerated emergency runs outside committed operations will be billed as ad-hoc professional services. I will include a brief statement of effort when I hand off the runbook.

Next steps (today):
1) Meditech confirms tenant ID + dataset hashes and preferred archive delivery method.
2) Kimberly confirms DPA amendment language approval.
3) Ops will send the job-run manifest and ETA for the purge pass.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: meditech_erase_matrix_v1.xlsx, log-escrow-checklist.pdf
